🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin slipped below $83K as the Iran standoff lifted oil and yields, yet record ETF inflows and Strategy's largest-ever stack show institutional conviction holding firm. 🛢️ Bitcoin Slips Below $83K as Iran Standoff Lifts Oil Bitcoin fell to roughly $82,600 on Monday, down about 2% in 24 hours, after President Trump rejected Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude pushed toward $108. With 10-year Treasury yields at their highest since 2007, altcoins took the brunt — ZEC dropped 7% and DOGE 5% — as traders brace for Wednesday's PCE and Friday's payrolls data. Read full story 🔓 Bitget Reopens BTC Withdrawals After $387.5M Hack Bitget restored Bitcoin withdrawals at 08:00 UTC today, four days after suspected North Korean hackers drained about $387.5 million from its hot and warm wallets. ETH follows on Sept. 29, USDT on Sept. 30 and remaining assets on Oct. 2; the exchange says the exploited vulnerability is fixed and user balances are covered by its protection fund. More details ⚖️ California Bans Public Officials From Issuing Memecoins Governor Gavin Newsom signed AB 2409 on Sunday, barring California state and local officials from issuing memecoins and blocking platforms from offering official-linked tokens to residents from Jan. 1, 2027. He paired it with SB 1208, extending money-laundering laws to digital assets and expanding seizure powers, and openly framed the package as a rebuke of Trump's crypto ventures. Read more 🏦 Bitcoin ETFs Log $2.4B Week, Flipping 2026 Flows Positive U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs absorbed $2.4 billion in the week to Sept. 25 — the largest weekly haul since October 2025 — turning 2026 net flows positive at about $934 million after a $5.8 billion deficit in July. BlackRock's IBIT led with $1.2 billion, though daily inflows cooled from $999 million on Monday to $135 million by Friday. See details ☀️ Solana ETFs Post Record $188M Weekly Inflow U.S. spot Solana ETFs drew a record $188 million last week, with every fund posting inflows and Friday's $87 million marking the best day since launch. Bitwise's BSOL captured about $128 million, or 68% of the total, even as SOL trades near $119, roughly 60% below its all-time high.
